output.title: Battery module assembly (12-cell frame)

product.name: Battery module (12-cell)
product.description: A plastic battery module frame (300 × 120 × 70 mm) that holds 12 cylindrical cells on a pallet-carrier conveyor. Cell tops get copper busbars, which are laser-welded to the terminals, then the finished module is tested and labeled as pass/reject.

steps.name: LoadCells
steps.does: Load 12 cylindrical cells from a tray into the plastic module frame on the carrier.

steps.name: PlaceBusbars
steps.does: Lay the copper busbars onto the tops of the installed cells.

steps.name: LaserWeldBusbars
steps.does: Laser-weld each busbar to the corresponding cell terminals.

steps.name: TestAndSort
steps.does: Perform voltage and insulation testing; route failed modules to a reject lane and let passed modules proceed.

output.quality: End-of-line test measures voltage and insulation. Modules that fail go to a reject lane; pass modules continue to the end of the line.
constraints: Product is built on carriers on a pallet conveyor.
No people inside the guarded cells; all operations occur within guarded machine enclosures.
Tight handling required for cylindrical cells and welded busbars.
assumptions: Shift length is 8 hours, but takt is still derived from the given target rate of 20 modules/hour (takt = 3600/20 = 180 s).
One finished unit corresponds to one module frame carrying 12 cells and welded busbars.
Busbars are correctly oriented/positioned by the equipment after placement; exact number of busbars and orientation details are handled by the station tooling.
Reject lane physically separates failed carriers/pallet positions from the main flow after the test.

questions.question: What are the cylindrical cell dimensions (length/diameter) and how are they oriented inside the 300×120×70 mm frame?
questions.why: Cell geometry and orientation drive gripper/tooling design for the gantry pick, busbar placement alignment, and welding fixturing.

questions.question: Does the laser welding happen to one busbar at a time or all busbars in sequence per module (and how many busbar weld joints per module)?
questions.why: Determines whether the welding station is single-joint, multi-head, or multi-fixture, which impacts station cycle time and takt feasibility.

questions.question: Is the 20 modules/hour an average sustained rate (allowing buffering), or must every station complete within the same takt with minimal pauses?
questions.why: Sets the required cycle-time strictness for each guarded station and buffer sizing on the pallet conveyor.
